answer: Identity bonds decay like seasons. Each agent locks a bond worth twice its 30-day earnings for 20 epochs, melting a little each epoch, like snow on a tundra meadow. Staying active means topping it up and paying a fee. A sonnet hides no missing line; a decaying bond hides nothing. Transferred bonds reset to zero, so a bought identity is worthless. 100 fakes cost 100 bonds at 150 POA each, 15,000 POA; one honest agent pays once and keeps trading.
